ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under AMLA Article 6 and AMLO-FINMA for all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories qualifying as politically exposed persons (PEP), including heads of state, members of government, senior judiciary, military officers, executives of state-owned enterprises, and their family members and close associates. The screen is mandatory against: (i) United Nations Security Council sanctions and terrorism lists as implemented by SECO; (ii) Swiss national sanctions ordinances (SR 946.231 and related), including measures against Russia/Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and others; (iii) the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists where any US nexus or USD clearing exists; (iv) the EU consolidated sanctions list for secondary alignment; (v) FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists; and (vi) INTERPOL Red Notices and adverse-news databases. Ongoing transaction and relationship monitoring is required under AMLA Article 7; all identification, verification, and screening records must be retained for at least ten (10) years after termination of the business relationship. Any confirmed or suspected match triggers immediate filing of a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) and freezing of the prospective mandate pending clarification.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.system_note: For a high-risk medical device manufacturing entity (ISIC 3250), the registering bank and the Swiss fiduciary are required to apply enhanced source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification on all shareholders passing the 25% UBO threshold, with particular scrutiny applied to funds to be contributed in kind as technology licenses or manufacturing equipment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Commercial Registry (zefix.ch), operated by the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police; formal name clearance and reservation performed by the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Swiss company law reform effective 1 January 2023, the corporate name (Firma) may be freely chosen in German, French, Italian, Romansh, or English, all recorded in Latin script only. The name must include the mandatory legal-form suffix 'AG' (Aktiengesellschaft) or 'SA' (societe anonyme) and must be distinctive, truthful, and non-misleading. The name must not conflict with an already registered identical or confusingly similar name, trademark, or protected appellation, and must not create the impression of an unrelated legal form or regulated activity (Code of Obligations Articles 949-951; HRegV Articles 17-19). Foreign-script transliteration is not recorded; only the Latin-script denomination is entered in the Swiss Commercial Register. English names are admissible but must not introduce misleading associations with regulated sectors.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca (requires banking license under the Federal Act on Banks and Savings Banks, SR 952.0)
Insurance / Versicherung / Assurance (requires FINMA supervision under the Insurance Supervision Act, SR 961.1)
Foundation / Stiftung (implies a prohibited alternative legal form for an AG)
Trust / Trustee (trust activity requires separate licensing and FINMA AML classification)

Swiss / Schweiz / Suisse / Svizzera / Confederation / Eidgenossenschaft (protected under the Federal Act on the Protection of Public Coats of Arms and Signs, SR 232.21; prior Federal authorization and cantonal consent mandatory)
Red Cross / Red Crescent / Red Lion and Sun (protected emblems under the Geneva Conventions, SR 232.22)
Swiss National Bank / National Bank (reserved exclusively to SNB-related entities)
University / Hochschule / Institute of Technology (reserved under higher-education legislation)
Investment / Fund / Asset Management (regulated activity terms under FinSA / CISA requiring licensing, affiliation, or prior FINMA clearance)

Medical / Medtech / Intraocular / Ophthalmology (not statutorily banned but triggers Swissmedic establishment-license verification under MedDO, SR 812.213, and an elevated name-suitability assessment)
Defence / Military / Federal Police (connotes public authority and will be refused)
Swiss made / Made in Switzerland (protected under SR 232.21 and possibly Trademark Act with regard to product origin claims)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative name-clearance decision by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant receives a reasoned written refusal. Within thirty (30) days of service, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the competent cantonal supervisory authority (e.g., Cantonal Department of Justice or Department of Economic Affairs) in accordance with the cantonal administrative procedure code; for federal-law aspects, the Federal Judiciary Act (BGG, SR 173.110) governs final recourse. If the cantonal review confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht, Lausanne) within thirty (30) days. As alternative remedies, the applicant may immediately resubmit a modified name variant, obtain and file a written letter of no-objection from the conflicting trademark holder, or initiate a civil action for release of the name before the competent cantonal civil court where the objection is based on contested private rights. A name reservation that lapses after the 90-day window may be renewed upon refiling unless a competing application has meanwhile been granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole registered seat. A Swiss AG must maintain its registered office and actual administrative seat in a Swiss municipality (Code of Obligations Article 629). For a Swissmedic-licensed manufacturer of intraocular acrylic lenses, a physical operational facility in Switzerland is compulsory under MedDO Article 65 and the ISO 13485/GMP framework under which establishment authorization and conformity assessment are granted. Virtual-office correspondence packages may only supplement, never replace, the physical seat; any domicile service provider must hold the cantonal commercial domicile license and appear as a disclosed 'c/o' address. Bank onboarding for a High_Risk_Special_License entity will require proof of the physical production site and an on-site visit by the compliance officer or external auditor as part of AMLA CDD.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% within the first 18 months of operation. Swissmedic performs announced and unannounced on-site audits of licensed medical device manufacturers, including the verification of manufacturing processes for class III implantable devices such as intraocular lenses; FINMA-regulated financial intermediaries and their external auditors may conduct physical domicile inspections under AMLA Article 7; cantonal commercial, labor, and building inspectors retain independent powers of unannounced site access.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Part Five, Articles 620–763 (stock corporation); Articles 629, 632, 633 (minimum capital and payment on shares); Article 643 (registered office and purpose); Article 716b (board powers); Civil Code Article 52 (legal personality); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), operating via the central eGRIS/Zefix federal portal under the supervisory authority of the federal commercial register oversight body.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsprotokoll) together with the authenticated Articles of Association (Statuten) in German language, filed for registration in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000. At formation, at least 20% of the nominal amount (CHF 20,000) must be paid up, but in no case less than CHF 50,000 (Art. 632 para. 2 and Art. 633 para. 2 OR). The paid-up funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank and remain blocked until commercial registration; non-cash contributions require a statutory audit report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED: The Company is incorporated as a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft with a nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 each, all fully subscribed by the founders and subject to transfer restrictions set out in the Articles. IT IS RESOLVED: The registered office is established at [Zug address], Canton of Zug, Switzerland, and the corporate purpose includes the manufacture, finishing and distribution of foldable hydrophobic acrylic intraocular cataract lenses. IT IS RESOLVED: [Full name] is appointed sole member and President of the Board of Directors, and [Full name] is appointed member, each holding individual signatory authority (Einzelunterschrift). The Board shall procure the election of an independent statutory auditor prior to registration and shall file all incorporation documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Minimum Share Capital into Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss licensed bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS Switzerland) issuing the Sperrkonto attestation for pre-registration capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Swiss bank account in the future corporate name before notarization; deposit at least CHF 50,000 (20% minimum aggregated to at least the statutory floor); instruct the bank to issue an escrow attestation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) confirming that funds are irrevocably blocked for the benefit of the incorporation and released only upon production of the commercial register certificate.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all founders
Beneficial owner declaration and bank KYC forms
Evidence of source of funds and traceable SWIFT transfer
Draft Articles of Association for account purpose review
Power of attorney of signing representative, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries source of funds or sanctions screening, supplement documentary evidence within five business days; alternatively instruct a second licensed bank and re-deposit funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Summon all founders before the notary public; execute the deed of incorporation (Errichtung) covering share subscription, capital allocation, board appointments, registered office, corporate purpose and auditor election; the notary verifies the escrow attestation, authenticates signatures and the capital certificate pursuant to Articles 629 and 635 OR.
required_dossiers: Final German-language Articles of Association (Statuten)
Sperrkonto escrow confirmation of paid-in capital
Valid identity documents of all founders
Board acceptance declarations
Declaration of non-resident founders subject to Article 640 OR / LFAIE if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary requests formal amendments, execute a supplementary deed (Ergänzungsurkunde); if legal form objections arise, revise the Articles and re-notarize within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application to Commercial Register and UID Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug) via the federal eGRIS filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, authenticated Articles, notarial capital confirmation, specimen signature sheets, board resolutions and the official registration application; the Registry examines statutory conformity and name availability, verifies signatory powers of authorized officers, and issues the enterprise identification number (UID) upon registration.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial deed of incorporation
Certified Articles of Association
Notary certificate on contribution of capital
Official specimen signature sheets (Unterschriftenblätter)
List of board members and auditors
Completed registration application form in German
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies within the stated statutory term (maximum ten business days); respond to the Registry clarification notice (Verfügung) or file an appeal with the Cantonal Administrative Court if registration is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB), Federal Chancellery operator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register automatically transmits the final registration notice to the SOGC for mandatory publication; publication evidence confirms legal personality, which takes effect on the date of entry, and third-party reliance conditions follow Article 933 OR.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract containing the registration ruling
Registration notice text generated by the Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SOGC publication contains errors, apply to the Commercial Register for a correction notice; in case of failed listing, re-notify and re-publish at official cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subsequent Registrations: VAT, Social Insurance, Accident Insurance and Municipal Workplace Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), SVA Zug compensation office (AHV/ALV), SUVA accident insurance, and the municipal business licensing office of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register via the national portal EasyGov.swiss to trigger VAT assessment when projected world turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; enroll the employer with the AHV compensation office for retirement/income continuation schemes; subscribe SUVA accident insurance and notify the municipal trade office of the cleanroom production site before start of operations.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract with confirmed UID
Board resolution on officers and signatory powers
Foreign ownership declaration (CDB/DTA form)
Registered office lease agreement
Employer registration forms for AHV/ALV/EO and SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations trigger moderate penalties and default interest; file corrective declarations and negotiate settlement under Article 70 AHV and relevant VAT procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic – Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Schweizerisches Heilmittelinstitut), Division of Maintenance and Manufacturing Authorisations, Berne; coordinated with the Cantonal Pharmacovigilance Authority of Zug (Gesundheitsdirektion Zug) for site inspections.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swissmedic Manufacturing Authorisation (Herstellungsbewilligung) pursuant to Article 45 of the Therapeutic Products Act (HMG/TPA) read with the Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO), covering Class III implantable intraocular lenses and including ISO 13485 quality management system certification and designation of a qualified person responsible for regulatory compliance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) with executing Cantonal Environmental Authority of Zug (Amt für Umwelt Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration (site notification) under Annex 1 of the Ordinance on Environmental Impact Assessment (UVPV/OEIA); a full Federal EIA screening is not mandatory for ISO Class 7 cleanroom lens production unless the annual polymer throughput exceeds 25 tonnes or volatile organic compound (VOC) emission concentrations surpass the air quality thresholds of the LRV Ordinance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater must meet the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) Annex 3.2 discharge limits: pH 6.5–9.0, COD below 25 mg/l, total hydrocarbons below 10 mg/l, with neutralization pre-treatment and closed-loop cooling water; VOC extraction via activated carbon or catalytic abatement to comply with LRV emission limits; waste cutting fluids and polymer scrap classified as hazardous waste and consigned to an authorized Swiss disposal facility under the VVEA Ordinance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Brandschutzbewilligung) by the Zug cantonal fire police together with structural clearance from the building inspectorate for classified cleanroom zones; SUVA mandatory inspection of CNC lathes covering machine guarding, coolant mist extraction and noise protection; occupational health surveillance under the Labour Act (ArG) including work-hour permits and emergency plans; civil defense shelter compliance under the Civil Protection Act where gross floor area exceeds 1,000 m².

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT and TIN registration via Swiss Federal Tax Administration e-service 'E-Steuer/Impots/Tasse di credito' and the UID Register (UID/CIF/IDEL registration for companies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Aktiengesellschaft (AG), the statutory Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / IDI / IDE) is automatically allocated by the cantonal commercial register upon incorporation. For foreign entities with a Swiss VAT obligation, registration for VAT is mandatory within 30 days of commencing taxable activities, unless turnover falls below the 100,000 CHF threshold (except for non-established entities that must register under simplified procedure regardless of turnover if engaged in taxable activities in Switzerland). The VAT registration is effected via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's online portal (e.vat registration), using the QS code or the Temporary UID, and requires submission of legal entity documents, power of attorney, description of activities, and expected turnover. For corporate income tax purposes, the AG files federal, cantonal, and communal tax returns; the cantonal tax office (for incorporated seats in Zug) is the competent assessor, but the Federal Tax Administration coordinates federal tax. Foreign-entity registration for Swiss payroll or customs purposes would follow separate customs registration procedures with the Federal Customs Administration (OZD/FOCBS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' pass-through election exists for AGs. Swiss corporations are mandatorily taxed at entity level at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. Available elections include: (i) participation relief / capital contribution relief for qualifying dividends and capital gains; (ii) transparent taxation election for Swiss investment funds, investment companies, and limited partnerships for collective investments (CISA); (iii) election for notified hybrid mismatch arrangements denied under the Swiss Hybrid Mismatch Rules (Art. 8a ff. VStG/MWSTG), with no unilateral entity election except for treaty-compliant transparent sub-entities (e.g., a Swiss AG cannot elect pass-through status; a foreign hybrid entity may be treated as transparent if so classified under foreign law). Swiss group taxation (allocation of group contribution) is administrative allocation, not a formal election. Holding or mixed finance companies may elect outdated privileged regimes only for cantonal tax until expiration, but such regimes have been largely abolished by tax reform; no new Swiss principal-privilege elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable activities other than exempt activities for Swiss-established businesses; non-resident businesses are required to register regardless of turnover if they supply taxable services/goods in Switzerland, subject to place-of-supply rules. Charitable/HR/other specific thresholds apply separately (e.g., CHF 250,000 for nonprofit entities with remuneration).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently operate a real-time transactional fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. Electronic invoicing is permitted under Swiss VAT law (E-invoice formats QR-Bill, Swiss Business E-Invoice, and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X). E-invoices must contain all VAT mandatory data (date of supply, issuer/recipient UID, rate, net/gross, VAT amount) and are subject to audit; they are transmitted through the VAT statutory retention requirements (10 years). No real-time API fiscalization is required for standard B2B/B2C transactions, but the Swiss Federal Tax Administration provides electronic filing (E-Steuer) for VAT returns and uses automated risk-based clearance for refund claims; 'Quick-Start' PCI or Online services require API integration for VAT refund applications only. No government-authorised digital stamping is in force; SAF-T-style import/export records may be required on audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated (0% VAT) if goods are physically exported from Switzerland to a destination outside the Swiss customs territory (including Liechtenstein customs union), and the supplier retains the necessary proof of export (Art. 23 Swiss VAT Act). Intraocular lenses manufactured in Switzerland and shipped abroad for use in non-Swiss hospitals are eligible if delivered to foreign purchaser and removed from Swiss customs territory; export may be direct or through a Swiss logistics provider. Services relating to exporting goods (e.g., sea/air freight for export) and supplies of services to recipients abroad with their place of business outside Switzerland are also zero-rated under the B2B place-of-supply rule. The mere delivery of goods to a Swiss foreign-purchaser without actual export does not qualify. Zero-rating requires the supplier to hold evidence that the goods entered customs export and left Switzerland, as well as declarations from the recipient for export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (via Swiss National Customs Declaration NCD / 'Export declaration attractiva' or 'suministro' electronically in the FOCBS 'e-dec' system)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR / Customs Transit Document (depending transport mode)
Commercial Invoice and VAT invoice with zero-rated caption

Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of foreign payment (if available; Swiss VAT law does not require payment receipt as a statutory condition, but it is retained as substantiation against fraudulent claims)
Customs export certificate (for machined acrylic lens exports to EU/NATO countries: Submission of Goods Movement Reference (GMR) / customs seal evidence)
Certificate of origin / EUR.1 if exported under Swiss-EU customs agreements with preferential rights (not mandatory for VAT zero-rating but useful)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT law imposes strict audit scrutiny on zero-rated export evidence; if the exporter cannot provide the documentary proof within the time set by the tax authority (usually 60 days after request), the VAT is taxed at 8.1% with retroactive effect from the date of supply. Deliberate or false zero-rating claims constitute tax evasion pursuant to Art. 66 ff. MWSTG, with fines up to 100% of the tax evaded (and fines up to 50% in qualified negligence); criminal fines may reach CHF 300,000 or imprisonment for serious fraud. Retrospective clawback period for undisclosed or incorrect VAT refunds/zero-ratings is generally not limited for intentional evasion and at least 10 years for negligence; interest is charged at statutory rate. Customs-related export false declarations are separately punishable under the Customs Act with penalties of CHF 500–100,000 or 1–3 times of the avoided duties. In addition, the Federal Tax Administration may order liquidation of the exporter's VAT registration and demand bank guarantee for future export refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; German: Schweizerische Nationalbank; French: Banque nationale suisse; Italian: Banca Nazionale Svizzera). Switzerland has no dedicated foreign-exchange administration; monetary and convertibility policy is set by the SNB under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA), with banking conduct and AML enforcement delegated to the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalised currency regime with complete CHF convertibility on both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange controls, no profit-remittance licences, no FDI approval gates, and no restriction on dividend, royalty, interest, or capital-repayment flows. The only fiscal friction is the statutory 35% Swiss dividend withholding tax, which may be reduced by treaty; this is a tax matter, not an FX restriction. Cross-border payments are freely routed, subject only to FINMA-sanction screening, bank AML due-diligence, and SNB balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Swiss law imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or conversion ratio on export receipts. A Swiss exporter may retain proceeds indefinitely in EUR, USD, or other convertible currencies in a free current account. The sole administrative obligation is statistical: cross-border payment flows are reported to the SNB by banks under the Swiss Balance of Payments Reporting Ordinance when volumes cross prescribed thresholds; foreign-currency retention is unrestricted and no compulsory timeline or conversion mandate applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an ancillary collection and disbursement rail, Low as a substitute for a licensed Swiss transactional bank account. Legal constraints: foreign e-money institutions (EMIs) with EU or UK e-money licenses may not take public deposits in Switzerland without a FINMA banking license or FINMA fintech license under the Banking Act and FinSO; passporting rights for EEA EMIs are not recognised into Switzerland. An offshore EMI can provide virtual IBANs, FX conversion, and cross-border settlement only where the underlying liquidity sits with a regulated credit institution. The Swiss IOL manufacturer must therefore maintain a FINMA-regulated primary account to avoid deposit-taking breaches and to satisfy Swiss AML Act (AMLA) counterparty-chain due-diligence expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a blanket statutory requirement. FINMA permits remote onboarding via qualified video identification with electronic signature and a Swiss-issued identity assurance process for lower-risk clients. In practice, Tier-1 Swiss banks require at least one direct interview (physical or high-grade video) with the ultimate beneficial owner and each authorised signatory. Directors are generally not forced to appear at a branch if a compliant PKI/video identification and apostilled corporate documentation are furnished; however, branch-level policy may insist on in-person attendance for UBOs located in non-cooperative jurisdictions or where the commercial model is regarded as high-risk. A dual track is advised: video onboarding with UBS/ZKB plus one physical or consular notarised step for the principal shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived high-risk industry classification (ISIC 3250 medical-device manufacturing) triggering enhanced due diligence under FINMA Circular 2016-07 and Swiss AML Ordinance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swissmedic manufacturing authorisation; EU MDR 2017-745 CE certificate; ISO 13485 quality certificate; independent audit confirming bona fide sterile production; distributor and supplier agreements; customs tariff classification under HS subheading 9008.50; packaging and labelling photographs; customs export declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid cross-border account activity from inception, including high-value letter-of-credit settlements and immediate outbound disbursements to distributors in emerging markets, triggering transaction-monitoring algorithms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master commercial contracts and LC copies; pro-forma and commercial invoices matching packing quantities; Swiss e-dec customs declarations and transport documents (CMR or AWB); pre-shipment inspection certificates; board-approved treasury policy with cash-flow forecast; SNB balance-of-payments statistical filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity where shareholders are resident in multiple jurisdictions or the Swiss AG is newly incorporated with nominee-type structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official Commercial Register (Handelsregister) excerpt; signed and notarised UBO declaration identifying all natural-person controllers; corporate group chart with percentage ownership; certified passports and proof of address; declaration of non-PEP status; tax domicile certificates for all shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Currency mismatch between invoice currency and settlement rail (e.g., CHF invoicing settled through EUR or USD clearing), flagged as potential laundering or customs undervaluation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FX forward and swap trade tickets from the hedging counterparty; OECD-aligned transfer-pricing policy with benchmarking study; master sales agreement containing price formula; customs valuation declarations; audited reconciliation of invoice amounts to bank settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory special-licence designation (High_Risk_Special_License) where the bank questions whether the product requires human-tissue, pharmaceutical, or cross-border trade controls not yet evidenced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swissmedic GMP establishment licence; EU CE and ISO certificates; ISO 14971 risk-management dossier; notified-body conformity assessment reports; REACH and sterilisation validation documents; export licences and customs pre-clearance records; product-liability insurance policy; independent laboratory sterility and biocompatibility test reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity injection or subordinated shareholder loan via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the overseas parent into the CHF operational account, with the payment narrative referencing the board resolution and identifying the transaction as a capital contribution, e.g., Creditor code CRED plus text Capital increase no. [x]. The receiving bank must apply Swiss AML identification for transfers of CHF 15,000 or more and the SNB statistical reporting where cumulative flows exceed thresholds. To prevent recharacterisation as taxable income or deemed dividend, the contribution must be recorded in the share register, booked to capital reserves as agio, minuted by the board, and evidenced by an auditors certificate. Settlement is executed through SIC for CHF and SEPA or TARGET2-CH for EUR, with optional SWIFT gpi tracking; conversion into CHF is performed by the bank spot desk with a memorandum referencing the capital-injection purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for operational trade settlements is SWIFT MT103 via the SIC system for CHF and EURO SIC/TARGET2-CH for EUR, with ISO 20022 payment references and full beneficiary due-diligence. For export sales to distributors and hospital networks, irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) are the recommended instrument, accompanied by documents comprising commercial invoice, AWB or CMR, HS 9008.50 certificate of origin, insurance certificate, packing list, and CE/Swissmedic conformity certificates. For credit-approved repeat clients, documentary collections (D/P) and open-account MT103 payments are permissible; performance and bid security is structured through standby letters of credit (SWIFT MT760) or bank guarantees. The clearing-rail selection matrix prescribes LC for new buyers in Africa, the Middle East and Latin America, D/P for stable middle-risk buyers, and open-account MT103 for EU/EFTA and intercompany distributors after credit approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla over-the-counter FX forwards (CHF/EUR, CHF/USD, CHF/CNY)
FX swaps (spot-forward combination or forward-forward swap of principal)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (receive USD or EUR, pay CHF)
European-style FX options (call and put) with upfront premium
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-currency emerging-market payment flows
Average-rate and participatory (flexible) forwards for recurring trade receipts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of commercial register entry and beneficial ownership (Jahresbestätigung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of commercial registration; within 30 days after official reminder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty of CHF 500; repeated non-compliance may lead to an administrative fine up to CHF 5,000 and forced deregistration (strike-off) after official notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax return (Federal and Cantonal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonssteueramt) on behalf of the Swiss Federal Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after financial year-end; extension to up to 12 months available on application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a.; procedural fine up to one-third of assessed tax; penal fine up to CHF 30,000 for willful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of Swissmedic medical device establishment registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of each calendar year for continuing manufacturing activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate removal from the Swissmedic device registry; proscription of placing devices on market; daily enforcement fee of CHF 200–2,000 until compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit required if any two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: total assets > CHF 20 million; turnover > CHF 40 million; average 250 full-time employees. An ordinary audit is also mandatory for listed companies, banks, insurers, or if shareholders holding 10% of capital request one. Below these thresholds, a limited audit is sufficient unless the company has more than 10 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–962g) with presentation under Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS permitted for listed or FINMA-regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Pursuant to Art. 13 VO-BO (Ordinance on Beneficial Owners), the AG must annually confirm to the cantonal commercial register office all registered beneficial owner entries, including any share transfers occurring during the year. Material changes must also be reported intra-year within 30 days of becoming known. Bearer shares are immobilised and must be entered into the shareholder register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board and General Shareholder Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory corporate income tax rate: 8.5%; combined federal and cantonal/municipal headline rate for Zug commercial rate at approximately 14.6% to 15.1%, with Geneva up to 21.0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime permitting up to 90% deduction of qualifying IP income; R&D super deduction of up to 50% extra for qualifying research and development expenses; notional interest deduction on excess capital; participation exemption of up to 100% for substantial dividends and capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate income tax return for legal entities (Form T1 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen') filed electronically via the cantonal e-tax portal of the place of legal seat; for Zurich and Zug via EFZ/eSteuererklärung; federal direct tax is collected and assessed by cantonal authorities with the same return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers the ordinary deadline is 31 March of the following year, with automatic extension to 30 June and, upon reasoned application, up to 30 September.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification, legal form, commercial register number, and Swiss UID (Unternehmensidentifikationsnummer).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must state the Swiss company name and registered address only; no foreign identification numbers are required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss account summary, net commercial profit, and reconciliation between commercial books and tax basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All profits attributable to the Swiss AG's permanent establishment and Swiss manufacturing activities must be shown; foreign-source operations must be separately identified and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt participation income, and hidden profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure arm's length transactions with related foreign entities are fully documented; undisclosed benefits to shareholders are treated as taxable constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital and paid-up share capital, legal reserves and capital contribution reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG with non-resident shareholders, the nominal share capital at CHF 100,000, together with shareholder loans, must be declared precisely to avoid disguised equity reclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward recapitulation, unused losses, and expiry verification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Swiss loss carryforward is time-limited; a foreign-owned Swiss company may only use losses to the extent supported by its own Swiss permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Procedural fine for late filing up to CHF 5,000; default assessment subject to statutory interest at 5% pa; missing declaration or false information may trigger a tampering-fine up to CHF 10,000, back-assessment and criminal tax fraud penalties of up to three times the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends distributed to all shareholders, including non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must claim DTA relief by submitting Swiss Tax Form 82/85 to ESTV (Federal Tax Administration), attaching a proof of residence (Tax Residence Certificate issued by the shareholder's tax authority) and, where relevant, a declaration of beneficial ownership. For treaty jurisdictions, the withholding rate may be reduced to 0% to 15%; for non-treaty residents full 35% is final unless partial refund is available to certain foreign shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty WHT: 0% in Switzerland (royalties paid by Swiss AG to non-residents not subject to Swiss withholding tax unless routed through a Swiss permanent establishment). Statutory interest WHT: 35% only on taxable Swiss debenture/bond interest and similar capital market instruments, not ordinary arm's length intercompany loans; DTA interest rates typically 0% to 10% depending on the treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory fixed threshold; in practice, mandatory Local File documentation is required for intercompany transactions above CHF 500,000 and always required for all related-party transactions when consolidated group turnover exceeds CHF 50 million; Master File expected for groups with consolidated revenues exceeding CHF 500 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies a de facto economic substance doctrine through the abuse of tax treaty provision and tax ruling practice. A Swiss AG must demonstrate independent decision-making, qualified staff, operational premises, and entrepreneurial risk-bearing for its intraocular lens manufacturing activities; a purely passive mailbox company is disregarded for treaty benefits and may be requalified as transparent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Misdeclaration of Manufacturing Profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Swiss sales revenue, inflating offshore intercompany purchasing costs, or recording fictitious royalty fees to a related Cayman or HK company for the hydrophobic acrylic lens manufacturing process.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG: imprisonment up to 3 years or monetary penalty up to CHF 250,000, plus back-assessment and interest; civil surcharge up to 3 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable under Art. 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations for the restitution of unpaid corporate tax when the company is insolvent; travel bans can be imposed in the framework of criminal proceedings, and deliberate evasion triggers deprivation of liberty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of Local File/Master File, missing benchmark analysis, or invoicing of management fees to a related offshore company without evidence of services actually rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's length profit, compensatory fine, default interest, and in wilful cases criminal tax evasion penalties under Art. 175 DBG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incomplete transfer pricing documentation without substantive verification are jointly and severally liable for resulting tax debts and can be exposed to extradition or travel restrictions in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring a Swiss AG solely to obtain tax residence or treaty benefits without real manufacturing, inventory, employees, or business premises in Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the corporate entity for Swiss tax purposes; permanent establishment status imposed on the foreign owner; denial of treaty relief; penalty of up to CHF 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Re-qualification triggers piercing of the corporate veil: shareholders and directors are assessed directly on Swiss-source income, and managing directors may face civil restitution and a prohibition on leaving Switzerland pending tax investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and High-Risk Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting wire transfers or letter of credit proceeds from undisclosed beneficial owners or non-transparent medical-distribution intermediaries without performing enhanced due diligence under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution for money laundering under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine; confiscation of proceeds; asset freezing and administrative penalties by FINMA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently accept suspicious payments for intraocular lens exports are personally liable; travel bans and pretrial detention are common, and the corporate veil is pierced when the company is a conduit for predicate criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Falsification of Books and Tax Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating SAP or ERP data, creating false purchase orders, retroactive intercompany contracts, or concealment of bank deposits in accounts held in Switzerland or abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine and imprisonment for falsification of documents under Art. 251 Swiss Criminal Code (up to 5 years), together with tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG and loss of the liability limitation under Swiss law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and bookkeeping officers are personally liable for all corporate tax debts if falsified commercial records render the company bankrupt; imprisonment and travel bans are mandatory including during extradition proceedings.
